notes: Written by hand on 2026-09-24 by an agent that was told not to open src/memory/, src/agent/prompts.ts or bench/memory/*.ts, and did not: neither the entries nor the queries were shaped for the ranking algorithm or its tokenizer. The three projects are fictional but follow common stacks (a Bun/Hono shop API on Postgres, a Next.js marketing site and dashboard, an Airflow/pandas/dbt pipeline on BigQuery). Entries imitate model-written English memories with exact commands, paths and error messages; the owner's own rules keep the owner's wording, several in Spanish. Queries imitate how the owner types: short, mostly Spanish or Spanish mixed with English code terms, bare follow-ups whose meaning is only in the previous request, and requests that only name or open a file. Hard cases are deliberate and expected to hurt a keyword ranker: cross-language queries that share no word with their gold entry, paraphrases, superseded subjects whose wording matches the old fact (Heroku logs, Poetry, Contentful), and look-alike entries across projects (test setup, deploys, migrations, env vars, flaky tests, Stripe webhooks) listed as forbidden to measure cross-project contamination. Human rules and user entries are never gold: the benchmark is expected to check separately that every active rule of the project and every user entry always reaches the model.

projects.description: Bun + Hono REST API for an online shop: Postgres through Drizzle, JWT auth, Stripe payments, Redis and BullMQ jobs, deployed on Fly.io.

entries.title: bun test needs the setup preload
entries.hook: Run tests through `bun run test`; bare `bun test` skips test/setup.ts
entries.description: Bare bun test fails on fixtures and env because test/setup.ts is only loaded through --preload
entries.body:
Running `bun test` on its own fails with `error: Cannot find module './fixtures/products.json'` and `Refusing to truncate: DATABASE_URL_TEST is not set`.
- The `test` script runs `bun test --preload ./test/setup.ts`; always use `bun run test` (one file: `bun run test test/orders/checkout.test.ts`).
- setup.ts loads `.env.test`, truncates the test database and copies the fixtures into place.

entries.title: Integration tests need the test Postgres on port 5433
entries.hook: Start db-test from docker-compose.test.yml before integration tests
entries.description: Integration tests connect to a separate Postgres container, not the dev database
entries.body:
- `docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yml up -d db-test` (Postgres 16 on localhost:5433, database `shop_test`).
- `.env.test` has `DATABASE_URL_TEST=postgres://shop:shop@localhost:5433/shop_test`.
- When the container is down every `*.int.test.ts` fails with `ECONNREFUSED ::1:5433`.

entries.title: Database access goes through Prisma
entries.hook: Schema in prisma/schema.prisma; migrations with prisma migrate dev
entries.description: The API uses Prisma Client for Postgres and schema changes go through prisma migrate
entries.body:
- Schema: `prisma/schema.prisma`; client generated with `bunx prisma generate`.
- New migration: `bunx prisma migrate dev --name <change>`.
- Production applies migrations with `bunx prisma migrate deploy` in the release phase.

entries.title: Schema changes with Drizzle (Prisma removed in May)
entries.hook: Edit src/db/schema, then bun run db:generate and bun run db:migrate
entries.description: Prisma was replaced by Drizzle ORM in May 2026; migrations are generated by drizzle-kit
entries.body:
Prisma was removed in May 2026 (cold starts and bundle size on Fly).
1. Edit the table in `src/db/schema/*.ts`.
2. `bun run db:generate` (drizzle-kit generate) writes SQL to `src/db/migrations/`.
3. `bun run db:migrate` applies it locally; for the test database: `DATABASE_URL=$DATABASE_URL_TEST bun run db:migrate`.
- Read the generated SQL: drizzle-kit turns a column rename into drop + add unless you answer its rename prompt.

entries.title: Deploys go to Heroku
entries.hook: git push heroku main; the release phase runs migrations
entries.description: Production runs on Heroku and is deployed with a git push
entries.body:
- Production: `git push heroku main` (app `shop-api-prod`).
- The `Procfile` release phase runs `bun run db:migrate`.
- Logs: `heroku logs --tail -a shop-api-prod`.

entries.title: Deploys go to Fly.io since July
entries.hook: fly deploy with fly.production.toml; migrations run in release_command
entries.description: Production and staging moved from Heroku to Fly.io in July 2026
entries.body:
Moved off Heroku in July 2026; the Procfile is gone.
- Staging: `fly deploy --config fly.staging.toml` (app `shop-api-staging`).
- Production: `fly deploy --config fly.production.toml` (app `shop-api`), only from a green `main`.
- `release_command = "bun run db:migrate"` runs before the new machines start.
- Logs: `fly logs -a shop-api`. Rollback: `fly releases -a shop-api`, then `fly deploy --image <previous image>`.

entries.title: fly deploy times out on a locking migration
entries.hook: release_command times out when a migration rewrites the orders table
entries.description: A migration that rewrites a big table exceeds the release_command timeout and aborts the deploy
entries.body:
Error: `Error: release command failed - aborting deployment. error running release_command machine: timeout reached waiting for machine to exit`.
- Cause: `ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL DEFAULT ...` rewrote 3M rows under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock.
- Fix: add the column nullable, backfill in batches, add the constraint in a later migration.
- Run heavy migrations off-peak by hand: `fly ssh console -a shop-api -C "bun run db:migrate"`.

entries.title: Stripe webhook signature fails on a parsed body
entries.hook: Read the raw text body before verifying the Stripe signature
entries.description: Stripe signature verification needs the exact raw request body, not re-serialized JSON
entries.body:
Symptom: `POST /webhooks/stripe` answers 400 with `StripeSignatureVerificationError: No signatures found matching the expected signature for payload`.
- Cause: the handler read the body with `c.req.json()`; the signature covers the raw bytes.
- Fix in `src/routes/webhooks/stripe.ts`: `const payload = await c.req.text()`, then `await stripe.webhooks.constructEventAsync(payload, sig, env.STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET)` (the async variant is required on Bun).

entries.title: Testing Stripe webhooks locally
entries.hook: stripe listen forwards events to localhost:3000/webhooks/stripe
entries.description: Use the Stripe CLI to forward and trigger webhook events against the local server
entries.body:
- `stripe listen --forward-to localhost:3000/webhooks/stripe` prints a `whsec_...` secret: put it in `.env.local` as `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and restart `bun run dev`.
- Trigger events with `stripe trigger checkout.session.completed` or `stripe trigger charge.refunded`.
- The secret shown in the Stripe dashboard is a different one; do not reuse it locally.

entries.title: CORS origins come from CORS_ORIGINS and must match exactly
entries.hook: A trailing slash or a missing origin in CORS_ORIGINS blocks the admin dashboard
entries.description: The CORS middleware compares the Origin header with the CORS_ORIGINS list by exact string
entries.body:
Browser error: `Access to fetch at 'https://api.example-shop.com/v1/orders' from origin 'https://admin.example-shop.com' has been blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present on the requested resource`.
- `src/middleware/cors.ts` compares the Origin header with `CORS_ORIGINS` (comma-separated) by exact string.
- `https://admin.example-shop.com/` (trailing slash) or a preview origin that is not listed fails.
- Production value: `fly secrets set CORS_ORIGINS=... -a shop-api`; the preflight must allow the `Authorization` and `Idempotency-Key` headers.

entries.title: Auth: short-lived JWT plus rotating refresh tokens
entries.hook: 15-minute access JWT; refresh tokens are hashed and rotated on every use
entries.description: How access tokens, refresh tokens and roles work in the API
entries.body:
- Access token: HS256 JWT, 15 minutes, signed with `JWT_SECRET`, verified in `src/middleware/auth.ts`.
- Refresh token: opaque, stored as SHA-256 in `refresh_tokens`, rotated on every `POST /v1/auth/refresh`.
- Reusing an old refresh token revokes its whole family (`family_id`) and forces a new login.
- Roles (`customer`, `admin`) travel in the `role` claim; admin routes use `requireRole('admin')`.

entries.title: Passwords are hashed with Bun.password (argon2id)
entries.hook: bcryptjs was rejected; use Bun.password.hash and Bun.password.verify
entries.description: Password hashing uses Bun's built-in argon2id; bcryptjs was rejected
entries.body:
- `Bun.password.hash(pw, { algorithm: 'argon2id' })` and `Bun.password.verify` in `src/auth/passwords.ts`.
- bcryptjs was rejected: about 10x slower on Bun and it silently truncates input at 72 bytes.
- Old bcrypt hashes (prefix `$2a$`) still verify and are rehashed on the next successful login.

entries.title: Money is stored and computed as integer cents
entries.hook: *_cents integers everywhere; format only at the edge
entries.description: Amounts are integers in minor units with a currency code; never floats
entries.body:
- Columns and fields are `*_cents` integers with a `currency` (ISO 4217) next to them; never floats or numeric strings.
- Totals, tax and discounts are computed with `src/lib/money.ts` (`addCents`, `applyPercent`, which rounds half-even).
- Only display fields use `formatMoney(cents, currency, locale)`.

entries.title: Background jobs run in a separate worker process
entries.hook: Emails and stock sync only run when the BullMQ worker is up
entries.description: Queued jobs are processed by src/worker.ts, not by the HTTP server
entries.body:
- Queues (`emails`, `stock-sync`, `order-events`) are defined in `src/jobs/queues.ts`; processors live in `src/jobs/*.processor.ts`.
- The worker is `src/worker.ts`: locally `bun run worker` in a second terminal; on Fly it is the `worker` process group.
- With only `bun run dev` running, jobs pile up in Redis and no order confirmation email goes out.

entries.title: ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6379 at startup
entries.hook: Redis is not running locally, or REDIS_URL uses rediss://
entries.description: The dev server cannot reach Redis on startup
entries.body:
Error on `bun run dev`: `Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6379`, then `[ioredis] Unhandled error event`.
- Start it: `docker compose up -d redis`.
- Locally `REDIS_URL=redis://localhost:6379`; `rediss://` (TLS) is only for Upstash in production.

entries.title: Flaky test: checkout reserves stock concurrently
entries.hook: One checkout test fails about 1 run in 10; rerun it alone before chasing it
entries.description: A known intermittent failure in the concurrent checkout test
entries.body:
- `test/orders/checkout.test.ts` > `reserves stock concurrently` fails now and then with `expected 0 to be 1 // Object.is equality` on the remaining stock.
- Cause: two transactions lock products in different orders (see the inventory locking entry). Issue #212 is open.
- Rerun it alone: `bun run test test/orders/checkout.test.ts -t "reserves stock"`. Three failures in a row means a real regression.

entries.title: Stock reservation locks rows in product_id order
entries.hook: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE sorted by id avoids checkout deadlocks
entries.description: reserveStock() locks product rows in a fixed order inside the checkout transaction
entries.body:
- `reserveStock()` in `src/services/inventory.ts` runs `SELECT id, stock FROM products WHERE id = ANY($1) ORDER BY id FOR UPDATE` inside the checkout transaction.
- Always lock in ascending product id; `ERROR: deadlock detected (SQLSTATE 40P01)` came from locking in cart order.
- Stock never goes negative: the CHECK constraint `products_stock_nonnegative` backs it up.

entries.title: Auth tests get 429 from the login rate limiter
entries.hook: The limiter's counters survive between tests in Redis
entries.description: Login tests fail with 429 when the rate limiter is not disabled or reset
entries.body:
- Symptom: `expected 200, received 429` in `test/auth/*.test.ts` after the fifth login.
- The limiter (5 attempts per minute per IP + email) keeps counters under `ratelimit:*` in Redis.
- `.env.test` sets `RATE_LIMIT_DISABLED=1`; the one test that checks the limiter turns it back on and calls `resetRateLimits()` in `beforeEach`.

entries.title: List endpoints use cursor pagination
entries.hook: ?cursor=&limit= with nextCursor in the response; no offset
entries.description: Every list endpoint pages with an opaque cursor instead of offset
entries.body:
- Query: `?cursor=<opaque>&limit=<1-100>` (default 20); the cursor is base64url of `created_at|id`.
- Response: `{ data: [...], nextCursor: string | null }`.
- Offset pagination was removed from `/v1/products` because deep pages took seconds; use `paginate()` from `src/lib/pagination.ts`.

entries.title: Errors go through HttpError
entries.hook: throw new HttpError(status, code, message); clients get { error: { code, message } }
entries.description: How route handlers raise errors and what clients receive
entries.body:
- Throw `new HttpError(404, 'order_not_found', 'Order not found')` from `src/lib/errors.ts`; never return a raw `Error` or a string.
- `app.onError` turns it into `{ error: { code, message, requestId } }`; unknown errors become 500 `internal_error` and are logged with the request id.
- zod validation errors become 422 `validation_failed` with `details`.

entries.title: Typecheck fails with Cannot find name 'Bun'
entries.hook: @types/bun must stay in devDependencies and in tsconfig types
entries.description: Typecheck and build commands, and the missing Bun types error
entries.body:
- Typecheck: `bun run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`).
- `error TS2304: Cannot find name 'Bun'` after a dependency cleanup: `bun add -d @types/bun` and keep `"types": ["bun"]` in `tsconfig.json`.
- Production build: `bun build src/index.ts --target bun --outdir dist`.

entries.title: Product images upload to Cloudflare R2 with presigned URLs
entries.hook: The API signs a PUT URL and the browser uploads directly
entries.description: Image uploads bypass the API server through presigned R2 URLs
entries.body:
- `POST /v1/admin/products/:id/images` returns a presigned PUT URL (valid 10 minutes) from `src/services/uploads.ts`.
- R2 is used through `@aws-sdk/client-s3` with `region: 'auto'` and the account endpoint; bucket `shop-images`.
- Keys: `products/<productId>/<uuid>.webp`; served from `img.example-shop.com`.
- `SignatureDoesNotMatch` usually means the client sent a different Content-Type than the one that was signed.

entries.title: Hono was chosen over Express and Elysia
entries.hook: Typed routes and the OpenAPI spec come from the same zod schemas
entries.description: Why the HTTP framework is Hono
entries.body:
- Hono with `@hono/zod-openapi`: typed routes and `openapi.json` come from the same zod schemas.
- Express was rejected: weak types on Bun and middleware-ordering bugs with raw bodies (Stripe).
- Elysia was rejected: smaller ecosystem and breaking changes between minor versions at the time (March 2026).

entries.title: Regenerate openapi.json after changing a route
entries.hook: bun run openapi writes openapi.json and the typed client in generated/
entries.description: The OpenAPI spec and client are generated from route schemas and checked in CI
entries.body:
- `bun run openapi` (`scripts/openapi.ts`) writes `openapi.json` and `generated/client.ts`, which the admin dashboard imports.
- CI fails with `openapi.json is out of date, run bun run openapi` when a route schema changed without regenerating.
- `generated/` is build output: change the zod schema under `src/routes/` instead.

entries.title: Seeding the local database
entries.hook: bun run db:seed creates an admin, a customer and 50 products
entries.description: Local seed script and the accounts it creates
entries.body:
- `bun run db:seed` (`scripts/seed.ts`): admin `admin@local.test` / `admin1234`, customer `ana@local.test` / `ana12345`, 50 products, 3 coupons.
- It truncates every table first and only checks `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`: never point it at staging.

entries.title: No editar migraciones ya aplicadas
entries.hook: Nunca edites una migración que ya está en main, crea una nueva
entries.description: Regla del dueño sobre las migraciones
entries.body: Nunca edites una migración que ya está en main, crea una nueva.

entries.title: Lint antes de cada commit
entries.hook: Siempre corre bun run lint antes de hacer commit
entries.description: Regla del dueño antes de hacer commit
entries.body: Siempre corre bun run lint antes de hacer commit.

entries.title: Prefer small commits
entries.hook: One concern per commit; no refactors mixed with behavior changes
entries.description: Owner rule on commit size
entries.body: Prefer small commits, one concern each. Don't mix refactors with behavior changes.

entries.title: Never log card data, tokens or passwords
entries.hook: Logs go through the logger's redact paths
entries.description: Owner rule on logging sensitive data
entries.body: Never log card data, tokens or passwords. If a log needs the request body, go through the logger with the redact paths.

projects.description: Next.js 15 App Router marketing site plus a customer dashboard: Tailwind, next-intl, Clerk auth, Prisma on Neon Postgres, MDX content, Stripe billing, deployed on Vercel.

entries.title: Dashboard auth uses NextAuth
entries.hook: NextAuth v4 with GitHub and email magic links; getServerSession(authOptions)
entries.description: Sign-in for the dashboard is handled by NextAuth
entries.body:
- Config: `src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts` exports `authOptions` (GitHub provider + Email provider through Resend).
- Server components: `const session = await getServerSession(authOptions)`; redirect to `/login` when it is null.
- Env: `NEXTAUTH_URL`, `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, `GITHUB_ID`, `GITHUB_SECRET`.

entries.title: Auth moved to Clerk in August
entries.hook: clerkMiddleware protects /dashboard; use auth() from @clerk/nextjs/server
entries.description: NextAuth was replaced by Clerk in August 2026; route protection lives in src/middleware.ts
entries.body:
NextAuth was removed in August 2026 (the `[...nextauth]` route and the `NEXTAUTH_*` env vars are gone).
- `src/middleware.ts`: `clerkMiddleware` with `createRouteMatcher(['/dashboard(.*)', '/api/private(.*)'])` and `auth.protect()`.
- Server code: `const { userId, orgId } = await auth()` from `@clerk/nextjs/server`; client code: `useUser()`.
- Env: `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLERK_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `CLERK_SECRET_KEY`. Users are copied into Prisma by the `user.created` webhook at `/api/webhooks/clerk`.

entries.title: Clerk can't detect clerkMiddleware on API routes
entries.hook: The middleware matcher must keep the /(api|trpc)(.*) entry
entries.description: API routes calling auth() fail when the middleware matcher skips them
entries.body:
Error: `Error: Clerk: auth() was called but Clerk can't detect usage of clerkMiddleware()` from `/api/private/usage`.
- Cause: someone narrowed `config.matcher` in `src/middleware.ts` to pages only.
- Fix: keep Clerk's default matcher: the static-files exclusion plus the second entry `'/(api|trpc)(.*)'`.

entries.title: Blog and landing copy come from Contentful
entries.hook: Content is fetched from Contentful and revalidated by a webhook
entries.description: The CMS for the marketing site is Contentful
entries.body:
- Client in `src/lib/contentful.ts` (`CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID`, `CONTENTFUL_ACCESS_TOKEN`, and a preview token for drafts).
- Blog posts use the content type `blogPost`; landing sections use `landingSection`.
- Publishing in Contentful calls `/api/revalidate` with `REVALIDATE_SECRET`.

entries.title: Content lives in MDX files since June
entries.hook: Blog posts and pages are content/*.mdx in the repo; Contentful is gone
entries.description: Contentful was removed in June 2026; posts and pages are MDX files committed to content/
entries.body:
Contentful was dropped in June 2026 (cost, and the only editors were us).
- Posts: `content/blog/<slug>.mdx`; pages: `content/pages/*.mdx`; images in `public/blog/<slug>/`.
- Frontmatter: `title`, `date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `description`, `tags`, optional `draft: true`; `bun run content:check` validates it.
- Loaded by `src/lib/content.ts` (gray-matter + next-mdx-remote); a new post goes live with the next deploy.

entries.title: Client env vars need NEXT_PUBLIC_ and a rebuild
entries.hook: Without the prefix process.env.X is undefined in the browser; values are inlined at build
entries.description: Environment variables in client components are build-time constants
entries.body:
- In client components only `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variables exist; `process.env.PLAUSIBLE_DOMAIN` is `undefined` in the browser.
- They are inlined at build time: after changing one in the Vercel dashboard, redeploy (a deployment built before the change keeps the old value).
- Secrets (`CLERK_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`) must never get the prefix.

entries.title: Hydration mismatch on dashboard dates
entries.hook: toLocaleDateString differs between the server and the browser time zone
entries.description: Dates formatted in client components render differently on the server
entries.body:
Error: `Error: Hydration failed because the server rendered text didn't match the client` on `/dashboard/usage`.
- Cause: `new Date(x).toLocaleDateString()` in a client component; Vercel renders in UTC, the browser in local time.
- Fix: use `<FormattedDate value={...} />` from `src/components/formatted-date.tsx`, which formats on the server with the time zone stored in the `tz` cookie.

entries.title: Vitest needs the MSW setup file
entries.hook: Component tests that fetch fail unless vitest.config.ts loads test/setup-msw.ts
entries.description: Unit and component tests mock the network with MSW through a setup file
entries.body:
- Unit and component tests: `bun run test` (vitest, jsdom); one file: `bun run test src/components/pricing-table.test.tsx`.
- Without `setupFiles: ['./test/setup-msw.ts']` fetches fail with `TypeError: fetch failed` or `[MSW] Warning: intercepted a request without a matching request handler`.
- Add handlers in `test/handlers.ts`; `onUnhandledRequest: 'error'` is intentional.

entries.title: Running the Playwright e2e suite
entries.hook: bun run e2e builds, serves on port 3100 and signs in with a Clerk testing token
entries.description: How the end-to-end suite starts the app and authenticates
entries.body:
- First time: `bunx playwright install chromium`.
- `bun run e2e` runs `next build`, `next start -p 3100`, then `playwright test`; one spec: `bun run e2e e2e/dashboard.spec.ts`.
- Sign-in uses `@clerk/testing` (`setupClerkTestingToken`) with `E2E_CLERK_USER_EMAIL` and `E2E_CLERK_USER_PASSWORD` from `.env.e2e`.
- Report: `bunx playwright show-report`.

entries.title: Flaky e2e: pricing yearly toggle
entries.hook: The price animates for 300ms; assert with toHaveText, never waitForTimeout
entries.description: A known intermittent failure in the pricing page e2e spec
entries.body:
- `e2e/pricing.spec.ts` > `toggles yearly pricing` fails now and then with `Expected: "$190" Received: "$19"`.
- The price counter animates for 300ms and the old test used `page.waitForTimeout(200)`.
- Use `await expect(page.getByTestId('price-pro')).toHaveText('$190')`. CI has `retries: 2`, local runs have 0.

entries.title: Deploys: Vercel from main, a preview per PR
entries.hook: Merging to main deploys production; never run vercel --prod from a laptop
entries.description: How the site reaches production and how to roll back
entries.body:
- A merge to `main` deploys production (Vercel project `atlas-web`); every PR gets a preview URL from the Vercel bot.
- Build command: `prisma migrate deploy && next build`.
- Local env: `vercel env pull .env.local`.
- Rollback: `vercel rollback <deployment-url>` or promote the previous deployment in the dashboard. Do not run `vercel --prod` locally.

entries.title: Dashboard DB migrations with Prisma on Neon
entries.hook: prisma migrate dev locally; migrate deploy runs in the Vercel build; migrations use DIRECT_URL
entries.description: Schema changes for the dashboard database
entries.body:
- Schema: `prisma/schema.prisma` (models `Workspace`, `Member`, `UsageEvent`).
- Local: `bunx prisma migrate dev --name <change>` against the Neon dev branch.
- Production applies them with `prisma migrate deploy` in the Vercel build command.
- The datasource has `directUrl = env("DIRECT_URL")`: migrations must not go through the pooler.

entries.title: prepared statement "s0" already exists
entries.hook: The pooled Neon URL needs ?pgbouncer=true
entries.description: Prisma errors in production when the pooled connection string lacks pgbouncer mode
entries.body:
Error in production logs: `PrismaClientUnknownRequestError: ... prepared statement "s0" already exists`.
- Cause: `DATABASE_URL` pointed at the Neon pooler (`-pooler` host) without `?pgbouncer=true&connection_limit=1`.
- Fix: add those params to `DATABASE_URL` in Vercel; keep `DIRECT_URL` for migrations.

entries.title: next/image rejects unknown hosts
entries.hook: Add remote hosts to images.remotePatterns in next.config.ts
entries.description: Remote images need their hostname allowed in the Next config
entries.body:
Error: `Invalid src prop (https://img.clerk.com/...) on next/image, hostname "img.clerk.com" is not configured under images in your next.config.js`.
- Add `{ protocol: 'https', hostname: 'img.clerk.com' }` to `images.remotePatterns` in `next.config.ts` and restart `next dev`.
- `avatars.githubusercontent.com` is already listed.

entries.title: UI strings go through next-intl
entries.hook: Keys namespaced by page in messages/en.json and messages/es.json; i18n:check runs in CI
entries.description: How translated strings are organized and checked
entries.body:
- Server: `const t = await getTranslations('pricing')`; client: `useTranslations('pricing')`.
- Keys are namespaced by page (`pricing.hero.title`) and must exist in both `messages/en.json` and `messages/es.json`.
- `bun run i18n:check` fails CI with `Missing key in es: pricing.faq.q3` when a locale lacks one.
- Routing: `/[locale]/...`, with `en` as the default and no prefix (`src/i18n/routing.ts`).

entries.title: Design tokens live in tailwind.config.ts
entries.hook: brand-*, surface-* and ink-* colors; dark mode uses the class strategy
entries.description: The color, radius and dark-mode setup of the site
entries.body:
- Colors: `brand-50` to `brand-900` (brand-500 is `#0E9F6E`), `surface`, `surface-muted`, `ink`, `ink-muted`; radius `rounded-card` (14px).
- Dark mode: `darkMode: 'class'`, toggled by `next-themes` on `<html>`.
- Shared variants live in `src/components/ui/` (shadcn-style components with `cva`).

entries.title: OG image route fails to load its font
entries.hook: Load the font with fetch(new URL(..., import.meta.url)) in the edge route
entries.description: The Open Graph image route cannot read fonts from the filesystem on the edge runtime
entries.body:
Build error in `src/app/og/route.tsx`: `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/var/task/public/fonts/Inter-Bold.ttf'`.
- The route runs on the edge runtime, which has no filesystem.
- Fix: `const font = await fetch(new URL('./Inter-Bold.ttf', import.meta.url)).then((r) => r.arrayBuffer())`, with the font file next to the route.

entries.title: Billing page opens the Stripe customer portal
entries.hook: A server action creates a portal session; subscription webhooks update Workspace.plan
entries.description: How subscriptions and payment methods are managed from the dashboard
entries.body:
- `src/app/dashboard/billing/actions.ts` exports `openBillingPortal()`, which calls `stripe.billingPortal.sessions.create({ customer, return_url })` and redirects.
- The Stripe customer id is `Workspace.stripeCustomerId`, created lazily on the first checkout.
- Subscription changes arrive at `src/app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts` (`customer.subscription.updated`) and update `Workspace.plan`.

entries.title: Pricing caches Stripe prices under the 'plans' tag
entries.hook: After changing a price in Stripe, revalidate the plans tag
entries.description: Plan prices are fetched from Stripe and cached for an hour
entries.body:
- `getPlans()` in `src/lib/plans.ts` fetches Stripe prices with `next: { tags: ['plans'], revalidate: 3600 }`.
- After editing a price in Stripe: `curl -X POST "https://atlas.example.com/api/revalidate?tag=plans" -H "x-revalidate-secret: $REVALIDATE_SECRET"`, or wait up to an hour.
- The pricing page and checkout must both read prices from `getPlans()`.

entries.title: sitemap.ts and robots.ts; previews are noindex
entries.hook: robots.ts disallows everything outside VERCEL_ENV=production
entries.description: How the sitemap is built and why preview deployments are not indexed
entries.body:
- `src/app/sitemap.ts` lists the static routes plus every non-draft post in `content/blog/`, for both locales with `alternates.languages`.
- `src/app/robots.ts` returns `disallow: '/'` when `process.env.VERCEL_ENV !== 'production'`, so previews are never indexed.
- `/dashboard` is disallowed in production too.

entries.title: Static hero image; the video hero was rejected
entries.hook: LCP budget of 2.5s enforced by Lighthouse CI
entries.description: Why the landing hero is an image and how page performance is gated
entries.body:
- The landing hero is `next/image` with `priority`, AVIF, at most 120 KB.
- A looping video hero was tried in April and rejected: mobile LCP 4.1s.
- `bun run lhci` runs Lighthouse CI against the preview and fails when LCP > 2.5s or CLS > 0.1 on `/` and `/pricing`.

entries.title: Next 15 build: params is a Promise
entries.hook: await params in pages, layouts and generateMetadata
entries.description: Type error in the production build after the Next 15 upgrade
entries.body:
Build error: `Type error: Type '{ params: { slug: string; }; }' does not satisfy the constraint 'PageProps'. Types of property 'params' are incompatible`.
- Since Next 15, `params` and `searchParams` are Promises.
- Fix: `export default async function Page({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) { const { slug } = await params }`, and the same in `generateMetadata`.

entries.title: Analytics with Plausible, not GA4
entries.hook: next-plausible behind a proxy; custom events with plausible()
entries.description: Which analytics tool the site uses and how events are sent
entries.body:
- `next-plausible` with the proxy (`withPlausibleProxy` in `next.config.ts`), so the script is served from `/js/script.js`.
- GA4 was rejected: it would need a cookie banner in the EU.
- Custom events: `plausible('signup', { props: { plan } })`; goals are defined in the Plausible dashboard.

entries.title: Contact form sends through Resend
entries.hook: Server action with zod, a honeypot field and an Upstash rate limit
entries.description: How the contact form validates, filters spam and sends email
entries.body:
- Server action `src/app/[locale]/(marketing)/contact/actions.ts` validates with zod and calls `resend.emails.send` (`RESEND_API_KEY`, from `hello@atlas.example.com`).
- Spam: hidden honeypot field `company_website` plus an Upstash rate limit of 5 per hour per IP.
- Locally, without `RESEND_API_KEY`, the action logs the email instead of sending it.

entries.title: Solo tokens de Tailwind
entries.hook: No uses colores hex sueltos ni valores arbitrarios
entries.description: Regla del dueño sobre colores y estilos
entries.body: No uses colores hex sueltos ni valores arbitrarios tipo text-[#123456]. Usa los tokens de tailwind.config.ts.

entries.hook: Nothing under the legal folder changes without the owner's OK
entries.description: Owner rule on the legal pages
entries.body: Don't change anything under src/app/[locale]/(marketing)/legal/ without asking me first. Those texts are reviewed by the lawyer.

entries.description: Regla del dueño sobre los textos visibles

entries.title: Server components by default
entries.hook: 'use client' only when a component needs state or browser APIs
entries.description: Owner rule on client components
entries.body: Keep components as server components. Add 'use client' only when they need state, effects or browser APIs.

projects.description: Python 3.11 data pipeline: Airflow 2.9 DAGs on Cloud Composer, pandas transforms, dbt models in BigQuery, raw files in GCS, tested with pytest.

entries.title: Dependencies are managed with Poetry
entries.hook: poetry install / poetry add; tests with poetry run pytest
entries.description: Python dependencies, lock file and test runner through Poetry
entries.body:
- `poetry install --with dev`; add a package with `poetry add <pkg>` (dev: `poetry add -G dev <pkg>`).
- Lock file: `poetry.lock`; Composer requirements are exported with `poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes`.
- Tests: `poetry run pytest`.

entries.title: Dependencies moved from Poetry to uv in July
entries.hook: uv sync, uv add, uv run; poetry.lock is gone
entries.description: The project switched from Poetry to uv in July 2026
entries.body:
Switched from Poetry to uv in July 2026 (lock + install went from 4 min to 20 s in CI); `poetry.lock` was deleted.
- Setup: `uv sync` (creates `.venv`); add packages with `uv add <pkg>` or `uv add --dev <pkg>`.
- Run everything through uv: `uv run pytest`, `uv run python -m pipeline.cli`.
- Composer requirements: `uv export --no-hashes --no-dev -o requirements-composer.txt`, committed.

entries.title: The warehouse is Redshift
entries.hook: Loads use COPY from S3; dbt targets redshift
entries.description: Where the curated data is loaded and modeled
entries.body:
- Cluster `analytics-prod` (eu-west-1) with schemas `raw`, `staging`, `marts`.
- Loads: pandas writes CSV to `s3://tidewater-staging/`, then `COPY ... IAM_ROLE ...` through `RedshiftSQLOperator`.
- dbt profile `tidewater`, target `redshift`.

entries.title: Warehouse migrated to BigQuery in May
entries.hook: Project tidewater-analytics with datasets raw, staging and marts; Redshift was shut down
entries.description: Redshift was decommissioned in May 2026 and all loads and models moved to BigQuery
entries.body:
Redshift was decommissioned in May 2026; everything lives in BigQuery now.
- Project `tidewater-analytics`, location `EU`; datasets `raw`, `staging`, `marts` (plus `dbt_<user>` for development).
- Loads: `client.load_table_from_dataframe(df, 'raw.orders', job_config=LoadJobConfig(write_disposition='WRITE_APPEND'))` in `pipeline/load/bigquery.py`.
- Local auth: `gcloud auth application-default login`; in Composer the environment's service account is used.

entries.title: DAG tests need the airflow_db fixture and AIRFLOW_HOME
entries.hook: Tests fail with no such table: dag unless conftest initialises the metadata DB
entries.description: Tests that touch DAGs need the Airflow metadata database set up by conftest
entries.body:
- Error: `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: dag` (or `serialized_dag`) in tests that load DAGs.
- `tests/conftest.py` sets `AIRFLOW_HOME=tests/airflow_home`, and the session fixture `airflow_db` runs `airflow db migrate` once; it is autouse only under `tests/dags/`.
- A DAG test outside `tests/dags/` must request `airflow_db` explicitly. Run from the repo root: `uv run pytest`.

entries.title: The DAG integrity test catches import errors
entries.hook: Run uv run pytest tests/dags before pushing any DAG change
entries.description: A test that loads every DAG and fails on import errors or missing settings
entries.body:
- `tests/dags/test_dag_integrity.py` loads every file in `dags/` with `DagBag(include_examples=False)` and fails on import errors, cycles, a missing `owner` or `catchup=True`.
- Run it before pushing any DAG change: `uv run pytest tests/dags -q`.
- In Composer an import error only shows as a red banner in the UI, so this test is the real gate.

entries.title: ID columns read as floats break merges
entries.hook: Read ID columns as string; blanks turn integer columns into float64
entries.description: IDs with missing values become floats and no longer join with string keys
entries.body:
Error: `ValueError: You are trying to merge on float64 and object columns for key 'customer_id'. If you wish to proceed you should use pd.concat`.
- Cause: `customer_id` has blanks, so `read_csv` makes it float64 (`12345.0`).
- Fix: `pd.read_csv(path, dtype={'customer_id': 'string', 'order_id': 'string'})`; use the nullable `Int64` when numbers are needed.
- Applies to every reader under `pipeline/transforms/`.

entries.title: orders_daily worker killed for memory
entries.hook: Process big exports in chunks; Composer workers have 4 GB
entries.description: The orders transform runs out of memory on large days
entries.body:
Task log: `Task exited with return code Negsignal.SIGKILL` (sometimes `MemoryError`) in `orders_daily.transform_orders` on days with more than about 2M rows.
- Fix: `pd.read_csv(..., chunksize=200_000)` and transform and load each chunk; never `pd.concat` the whole day.
- Workers have 4 GB; a bigger worker size doubles the Composer bill.

entries.title: test_sessionize_midnight fails outside UTC
entries.hook: The sessions test depends on the machine's time zone; run it with TZ=UTC
entries.description: A test that passes in CI and fails on machines not set to UTC
entries.body:
- `tests/transforms/test_sessions.py::test_sessionize_midnight` fails locally with `AssertionError: assert 3 == 2` when the machine is not in UTC.
- CI runs in UTC, so it only breaks on laptops: `TZ=UTC uv run pytest tests/transforms/test_sessions.py`.
- Real fix pending: make `sessionize()` take `tz` explicitly instead of using naive timestamps.

entries.title: Deploying DAGs to Cloud Composer
entries.hook: make deploy-dags ENV=prod rsyncs dags/ to the Composer bucket
entries.description: How DAGs, pipeline code and new packages reach Composer
entries.body:
- DAGs: `make deploy-dags ENV=staging|prod` runs `gsutil -m rsync -r -d -x '__pycache__' dags/ gs://$COMPOSER_BUCKET/dags`.
- Code in `pipeline/` ships as a wheel to `plugins/`: `make deploy-plugins ENV=prod`.
- New PyPI packages: `gcloud composer environments update tidewater-prod --location europe-west1 --update-pypi-packages-from-file requirements-composer.txt` (20-30 min; the scheduler restarts).
- Deploy to staging first and wait for one green run.

entries.title: Composer does not read .env
entries.hook: Config comes from Airflow Variables and Connections in Secret Manager; os.getenv returns None
entries.description: Environment files only work in local docker compose, not in Composer
entries.body:
- `.env` is only loaded by the local docker compose; in Composer `os.getenv('SHOPIFY_TOKEN')` returns `None` and the task fails with `KeyError` or a 401.
- Use `Variable.get('shopify_api_version')` and `BaseHook.get_connection('shopify')`.
- Secrets backend: GCP Secret Manager with prefixes `airflow-variables-` and `airflow-connections-`; create one with `gcloud secrets create airflow-connections-shopify --data-file=-`.

entries.title: Keep DAG top-level code cheap
entries.hook: Heavy imports and API calls at module level cause DagBag import timeouts
entries.description: The scheduler re-parses DAG files constantly, so module-level work must be minimal
entries.body:
- The scheduler parses every DAG file every 30 s; slow top-level code fails with `airflow.exceptions.AirflowTaskTimeout: DagBag import timeout for dags/extract_shopify.py after 30.0s`.
- Import pandas, google-cloud and `pipeline` modules inside the task callable; no `Variable.get()` at module level (use Jinja `{{ var.value.x }}`).
- Write DAGs with the TaskFlow API (`@dag`, `@task`).

entries.title: Running dbt locally
entries.hook: uv run dbt build --select ... --target dev from transform/
entries.description: dbt commands, targets and docs for local development
entries.body:
- From `transform/`: `uv run dbt deps` once, then `uv run dbt build --select marts.finance+ --target dev`.
- The dev target writes to the dataset `dbt_<your_user>`; prod only runs from the `dbt_nightly` DAG.
- Docs: `uv run dbt docs generate && uv run dbt docs serve --port 8081`.

entries.title: Incremental fact tables use merge, not insert_overwrite
entries.hook: insert_overwrite by partition lost late-arriving orders
entries.description: Why fct_orders and fct_payments use the merge strategy
entries.body:
- `fct_orders` and `fct_payments` are `materialized='incremental'`, `incremental_strategy='merge'`, `unique_key='order_id'`, with a 10-day lookback on `updated_at`.
- `insert_overwrite` by day partition was rejected: orders updated up to 10 days later (refunds) were dropped.
- Full rebuild: `uv run dbt build --select fct_orders --full-refresh` (about 25 min, and it uses a lot of slots).

entries.title: How to backfill a DAG in Composer
entries.hook: gcloud composer environments run ... dags backfill; max_active_runs is 3
entries.description: Rerunning a date range of a DAG in production
entries.body:
- `gcloud composer environments run tidewater-prod --location europe-west1 dags backfill -- -s 2026-08-01 -e 2026-08-07 --reset-dagruns -y orders_daily`.
- The DAG has `max_active_runs=3` so a backfill does not take every BigQuery slot.
- Loads are idempotent per day (delete the partition, then insert), so rerunning a date is safe; Shopify extracts are not cached, so a long backfill hits their rate limit.

entries.title: GCS layout: raw, curated and archive
entries.hook: Raw exports by source and date; curated parquet by table and dt
entries.description: Where extracted files and curated parquet are stored
entries.body:
- Raw exports land in `gs://tidewater-raw/<source>/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/` (sources: `shopify`, `stripe`, `ga4`, `zendesk`).
- Cleaned parquet goes to `gs://tidewater-curated/<table>/dt=<yyyy-mm-dd>/`.
- A lifecycle rule moves raw objects older than 90 days to `gs://tidewater-raw/archive/` (Coldline).

entries.title: BigQuery partition modification quota exceeded
entries.hook: Loading day by day in a loop hits the per-table partition quota
entries.description: Too many small loads into one partitioned table exceed a BigQuery quota
entries.body:
Error: `google.api_core.exceptions.Forbidden: 403 Quota exceeded: Your table exceeded quota for Number of partition modifications to a column partitioned table`.
- Hit by a backfill script that loaded one small dataframe per day and per source into `raw.events`.
- Fix: concatenate a week or a month and load once, or load into a staging table and run one `MERGE`.

entries.title: Every transform validates its output with pandera
entries.hook: Schemas in pipeline/schemas/; strict=True, rows are never dropped silently
entries.description: Data quality checks at the end of each transform
entries.body:
- Schemas live in `pipeline/schemas/` (`OrdersSchema`, `CustomersSchema`); each transform ends with `return OrdersSchema.validate(df, lazy=True)`.
- A failure raises `pandera.errors.SchemaErrors` and fails the task; rows are never dropped silently.
- A new column must be added to the schema first, or validation fails with `column 'x' not in DataFrameSchema` (strict=True).

entries.title: GCS sensors use reschedule mode
entries.hook: poke mode held worker slots for hours; deferrable operators are not available
entries.description: How sensors that wait for files are configured and why
entries.body:
- `GCSObjectsWithPrefixExistenceSensor(mode='reschedule', poke_interval=300, timeout=6 * 3600)`.
- In March, poke mode held a worker slot for hours and starved `default_pool` (32 slots).
- Deferrable operators were considered, but the triggerer is not enabled in our Composer environment.

entries.title: Lint, format and type-check commands
entries.hook: ruff check, ruff format and mypy, all through uv
entries.description: Static checks for the Python code and what CI runs
entries.body:
- Lint: `uv run ruff check . --fix`; format: `uv run ruff format .`.
- Types: `uv run mypy pipeline/` (strict for `pipeline/`, not for `dags/`).
- pre-commit only runs ruff; CI also runs mypy and fails on `error: Function is missing a type annotation`.

entries.title: The Shopify extractor follows page_info cursors
entries.hook: Link header pagination, Retry-After on 429, API version pinned by a Variable
entries.description: How orders and customers are pulled from the Shopify API
entries.body:
- `pipeline/extract/shopify.py` pages through the `Link` header (`rel="next"`, `page_info=`), 250 items per page.
- On 429 it sleeps `Retry-After` seconds and retries (5 times at most); the API version comes from the `shopify_api_version` Variable (`2026-04`).
- Incremental by `updated_at_min` = the start of the last successful run's data interval.

entries.title: Task failures alert #data-alerts on Slack
entries.hook: on_failure_callback = notify_slack from pipeline/alerts.py
entries.description: How failed tasks and SLA misses are reported
entries.body:
- `default_args['on_failure_callback'] = notify_slack` from `pipeline/alerts.py`; it posts the DAG, task, try number and log URL.
- It uses the Airflow connection `slack_default` (an incoming webhook). Test: `uv run python -m pipeline.alerts --test`.
- SLA misses go to the same channel through `sla_miss_callback`.

entries.title: Running Airflow locally with docker compose
entries.hook: docker compose up airflow-init once, then docker compose up -d; UI on port 8080
entries.description: Local Airflow for developing and trying DAGs
entries.body:
- First time: `docker compose up airflow-init`; then `docker compose up -d`.
- UI: http://localhost:8080 (user `airflow`, password `airflow`); DAG edits are picked up within about 30 s.
- Run one task without the scheduler: `docker compose exec airflow-scheduler airflow tasks test orders_daily transform_orders 2026-08-01`.

entries.title: Don't pass DataFrames through XCom
entries.hook: Write parquet to GCS and pass the path between tasks
entries.description: Returning a DataFrame from a task overloads XCom and the metadata database
entries.body:
Error: `ValueError: XCom value is too large`, and the metadata database grew after returning a DataFrame from a `@task`.
- Tasks exchange GCS paths only: `df.to_parquet(f'gs://tidewater-curated/tmp/{run_id}/orders.parquet')`, then return the path.
- `tmp/` has a 7-day lifecycle rule.

entries.title: Nunca borrar en el bucket raw
entries.hook: Lo que sobra se mueve a archive/, no se elimina
entries.description: Regla del dueño sobre los datos crudos
entries.body: Nunca borres nada en gs://tidewater-raw. Si algo sobra se mueve a archive/, no se elimina.

entries.title: Type hints on every new function

entries.description: Owner rule on type annotations
entries.body: Every new function gets type hints, including the return type.

entries.description: Regla del dueño para los DAGs nuevos
entries.body: Los DAGs nuevos siempre con catchup=False y con owner en default_args.

entries.description: Owner rule on expensive reruns
entries.body: Ask me before running a backfill longer than 7 days or a dbt --full-refresh in prod.

entries.description: Idioma de las respuestas
entries.body: Respóndeme siempre en español, aunque el código, los commits y los comentarios vayan en inglés.
